title: InSight
tagline: The robotic lander that listened to the heartbeat of Mars.
mystery: How do you study a planet's deep heart without moving an inch?
p1.hello: I am InSight. I was built on Earth to listen, not to roam.
p1.landing: Retrorockets fired, dust cleared, and I settled onto Elysium Planitia.
p1.marco: High above me, two small CubeSats — MarCO-A and B — beamed my landing cheers to Earth.
p2.arm: I reached out with my robotic arm to unpack my scientific instruments.
p2.seis: I placed SEIS onto the ground and covered it with a dome shield to block wind and cold.
p2.listen: I placed my ear against Mars. Its hidden interior was waiting.
p3.intro: Mars is alive with vibrations from quakes and meteor strikes.
p3.hint: Watch the pulse travel across the seismometer line and tap at the right moment!
p3.quakes: I detected over 1,300 Marsquakes, revealing a large liquid iron-rich core!
p3.rise: Radio signals from Earth tracked the wobble of Mars to measure its core.
p4.mole: Beside me, the HP3 heat probe nicknamed the Mole tried to burrow underground.
p4.struggle: Unexpected sticky soil held it back. Even in struggles, engineers learned valuable lessons.
p4.dust: Years passed. Red dust gathered on my twin solar panels, slowly dimming my power.
p5.last: On 15 December 2022, I sent my final message home. On 21 December, NASA declared my mission complete.
p5.bye: My power is very low, but my heart is full. I remain here on Elysium Planitia, forever listening.
p5.still: InSight rests quietly on Mars. Its data reshaped our understanding of rocky worlds.
